Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like the second half of 2013, probably after the taper tantrum.

- The unemployment rate was 7.3% in Aug-Sep 2013 and 7.0% in Dec 2013. A reading of 7.6% matches May-June 2013 (7.5% in May, 7.6% in April?). The 2013 series ran roughly: Jan 7.9, Feb 7.7, Mar 7.6, Apr 7.5, May 7.5, Jun 7.5, Jul 7.3. So 7.6% looks like March 2013, but the 10-year yield change of +0.93 over 3 months points to later.
- The 10-year yield was 2.63% around end-August 2013 (about 2.78%) and end-June 2013 (2.52%). End-July 2013 was 2.58%. The 3-month rise of 0.93 fits June-August, since the 10-year was about 1.7% in May. The 12-month rise of 1.12 fits too, because the 10-year was about 1.5% in mid-2012.
- Gold fell 21% over 6 months and 9.3% over 3 months, but gained 5.6% in 1 month. That fits July 2013, when gold rebounded from the June low.
- US equities were up 4.6% in the month, which matches July 2013 (+5.1%). The 24% 12-month return fits too.
- The unemployment rate of 7.6% may be the unrevised June figure. Its 12-month change of -0.6 implies a year earlier of 8.2%, which matches July 2012. So the snapshot is July 2013 and the rate would be 7.4%, but the data may be vintage-adjusted.
- Core CPI at 1.64% and headline at 1.76% fit mid-2013.

I settle on July 2013.
